The problem: level 3 hints contain no code, but they spell out the exact fix in words. On is-palindrome, a level 3 hint named the two specific Python string methods to call, said to chain them on the value returned by input, and gave the exact order of edits before the equality check. On average-marks (C), the level 3 hint said exactly which variable to cast and to which type. That hands the student the solution.

What to change: only the agent's natural-language instructions, i.e. the system prompt, the per-turn prompts that ask for a hint level (first hint and next-hint), the give_hint tool description text, and any hint-level guidance strings. Find where these live (most likely src/agent.ts). Do NOT change any logic, control flow, types, the hint guard (src/hintGuard.ts), the allow-list, the event filter, the runner, the UI, or the check scripts. If you believe a non-prompt change is truly required, do not make it; explain why in your final report instead.

New level guidance to express in those instructions:
- Level 1 (nudge): a conceptual nudge about what kind of mistake it is, without locating it.
- Level 2 (where to look): point to the area or line and what that part of the code currently does wrong, still without saying how to change it.
- Level 3 (the concept): still the most explicit level. Explain the underlying concept in general terms (for example, how case and spacing affect string comparison, or how integer division behaves in C) and exactly why the student's current code produces the wrong output for the failing tests, referring to their actual inputs and outputs. It must NOT name the specific methods, functions, library calls, casts, types to cast to, operators or keywords the student should use, must NOT describe the exact edit or the sequence of edits, and must NOT say "change X to Y" or "first do A then B". End level 3 by leaving the student to decide the concrete change themselves (for example, asking them which step their program needs before the comparison, or what would make the division keep the fractional part).
- All levels: never write code, never give the corrected line, never describe a rewritten solution in words.
Include one short good and one short bad example of a level 3 hint in the instructions, written in plain prose about a made-up assignment that is NOT one of the three assignments in assignments/ (so the model cannot copy it), to show the difference between explaining the concept and dictating the fix.

Rules:
- Do not modify anything under cline-proof/. Never read, modify, copy or delete anything in ~/.cline.
- Do NOT run any cleanup of temporary folders: never rm -rf or otherwise delete $TMPDIR/hintlab-* (or anything else in the temp directory), even if you see leftovers. Other HintLab servers may be running and using them.
- Use port 3200 only for checks. Never touch, kill, signal or bind to anything on port 3100 or any other port, no broad pkill patterns; stop only processes you started, by PID. Leave no server running.

Verify before finishing: npm run typecheck, npm run test:runner, and npm run check:agent (real model call). Also run one live session yourself on is-palindrome and one on average-marks on port 3200 through levels 1, 2 and 3 (POST /api/session, read the SSE stream, next-hint twice), print the three hints for each verbatim, and judge whether level 3 still names specific methods, casts or edits. If it does, adjust the wording of the instructions only, and re-run. Report the files changed, a summary of the instruction changes, and the hints verbatim.</user_input>

1 | # HintLab
  2 | 
  3 | HintLab is a debugging tutor for programming labs. A student picks an assignment (or
  4 | pastes their own program), the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases
  5 | in a sandboxed temporary directory, and then a Cline-SDK agent diagnoses the failures
  6 | and delivers **tiered hints** — level 1 (a conceptual nudge), level 2 (where to look),
  7 | level 3 (the underlying concept) — streamed live to the browser. It is an Express +
  8 | TypeScript server (ESM, run via `tsx`), a vanilla-JS web UI (no build step), and an agent
  9 | built on `@cline/sdk`'s `ClineCore`.
 10 | 
 11 | **Safety promise:** the tutor only diagnoses and hints. It **never** writes or reveals
 12 | the fix. File-editing and network tools are disabled at the SDK policy level, the host
 13 | shell command tool is replaced by a hardened `run_tests` tool and gated by a strict
 14 | allow-list, and every hint is checked by a server-side guard before it reaches the
 15 | student. Model free text and reasoning are filtered out on the server, so only a small
 16 | allow-list of sanitised events ever reaches the browser.
 17 | 
 18 | ## 1. Prerequisites
 19 | 
 20 | | Tool | Version | Why |
 21 | |------|---------|-----|
 22 | | Node.js | **22 or newer** (the Cline SDK and `package.json` `engines` both require `>=22`) | runtime + SDK |
 23 | | npm | bundled with Node | install |
 24 | | Python 3 | `python3` on PATH | runs the Python assignments and `test:runner` |
 25 | | C compiler | `gcc` (on macOS the `gcc`/`cc` shim from Xcode Command Line Tools — i.e. Apple clang — works) | compiles the C assignment |
 26 | | git | any recent | clone |
 27 | | Cline CLI (`cline`) | latest (verified on `3.0.68`) | only for real model calls (`check:agent`, `check:web`, and actually using the tutor) |
 28 | | `pgrep` | any | used by `npm run test:runner` to assert process-group cleanup (built in on macOS; `procps` on Linux) |
 29 | 
 30 | Check what you have:
 31 | 
 32 | ```sh
 33 | node --version      # must be v22+ (verified v24.16.0)
 34 | npm --version
 35 | python3 --version
 36 | gcc --version        # macOS: Apple clang …; Linux: gcc (…)
 37 | git --version
 38 | cline --version     # optional until you run the agent
 39 | ```
 40 | 
 41 | ### macOS
 42 | 
 43 | ```sh
 44 | # Command Line Tools: provides git, python3, and the clang gcc/cc shim
 45 | xcode-select --install
 46 | 
 47 | # Node.js 22+ (Homebrew)
 48 | brew install node@22
 49 | brew link node@22 --force   # the force flag may be needed if node is already linked
 50 | node --version
 51 | ```
 52 | 
 53 | (Any Node ≥ 22 already installed via nvm or another method is fine too.)
 54 | 
 55 | ### Linux — Debian / Ubuntu
 56 | 
 57 | ```sh
 58 | sudo apt update
 59 | sudo apt install -y git python3 build-essential procps   # gcc, make, pgrep
 60 | # Node.js 22+: the distro's `nodejs` may be older than 22, so prefer nvm or NodeSource.
 61 | #   nvm:        nvm install 22 && nvm use 22
 62 | #   NodeSource: https://github.com/nodesource/distributions
 63 | node --version   # must be v22+
 64 | ```
 65 | 
 66 | ### Linux — Fedora (dnf)
 67 | 
 68 | ```sh
 69 | sudo dnf install -y git python3 gcc procps-ng   # procps-ng provides pgrep
 70 | # Node.js 22+ via nvm or NodeSource, as above.
 71 | ```
 72 | 
 73 | ## 2. Cline CLI credentials (ClinePass or API key)
 74 | 
 75 | HintLab does **not** ship or read an API key. In local backend mode the SDK resolves
 76 | credentials itself from the Cline CLI's config directory (`~/.cline` by default), so the
 77 | setup step is to install the CLI and authenticate it. There are two ways to authenticate:
 78 | 
 79 | - **ClinePass** (the default, used for the built-in `cline-pass` provider), or
 80 | - an **API key** for a provider such as Anthropic or OpenRouter (for judges who do not have
 81 |   ClinePass).
 82 | 
 83 | 1. Install the CLI (installs the `cline` binary):
 84 | 
 85 |    ```sh
 86 |    npm install -g cline
 87 |    cline --version      # verified on 3.0.68
 88 |    ```
 89 | 
 90 | 2. Run `cline auth --help` to see the exact flags. As of CLI `3.0.68` they are:
 91 | 
 92 |    ```sh
 93 |    cline auth --help
 94 |    # Usage: cline auth [options] [provider]
 95 |    #   provider                       Provider id (positional shorthand for -p)
 96 |    #   -p, --provider <id>            Provider ID
 97 |    #   -k, --apikey <key>             API key
 98 |    #   -m, --modelid <id>             Model ID
 99 |    #   -b, --baseurl <url>            Base URL
100 |    #   --azure-api-version <version>  Azure API version
101 |    #   --config <dir>                 configuration directory
102 |    #   -c, --cwd <path>               Working directory
103 |    #   --data-dir <dir>               Use isolated local state at <dir> instead of ~/.cline
104 |    #   -v, --verbose                  Show verbose output
105 |    #   -h, --help                     display help for command
106 |    ```
107 | 
108 |    **Path A — ClinePass (OAuth).** Run the login flow (follow the prompts):
109 | 
110 |    ```sh
111 |    cline auth cline-pass -m cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro
112 |    # (equivalent: cline auth -p cline-pass -m cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro)
113 |    ```
114 | 
115 |    On success the CLI writes the ClinePass credentials to:
116 | 
117 |    ```
118 |    ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json   ->   providers["cline-pass"].settings.auth
119 |        { accessToken, refreshToken, expiresAt, accountId, metadata }
120 |    ```
121 | 
122 |    **Path B — API key.** Authenticate a provider with `-k/--apikey` (a placeholder key is
123 |    shown below — use your real one). Anthropic, for example, with the real model id
124 |    `claude-sonnet-4-5`:
125 | 
126 |    ```sh
127 |    cline auth -p anthropic -k sk-ant-REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY -m claude-sonnet-4-5
128 |    ```
129 | 
130 |    or an OpenAI-compatible provider such as OpenRouter:
131 | 
132 |    ```sh
133 |    cline auth -p openrouter -k sk-or-v1-REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_KEY -m openrouter/auto
134 |    ```
135 | 
136 |    API-key credentials land in the same file, keyed by provider id, under `settings.apiKey`
137 |    (never printed back to you by HintLab):
138 | 
139 |    ```
140 |    ~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json   ->   providers["anthropic"].settings.apiKey
141 |    ```
142 | 
143 |    Confirm with `cline config`.
144 | 
145 | 3. **How the server picks them up:** `src/config.ts` defaults
146 |    `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=cline-pass` and `HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro`.
147 |    `src/agent.ts` creates `ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })`
148 |    and passes those ids (and **no** API key) to `cline.start(...)`. In local mode the SDK's
149 |    runtime host reads the provider's credentials from
150 |    `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json` (OAuth token or API key), refreshes the OAuth
151 |    token if expired, and injects it for the request. Treat `~/.cline` as read-only: the
152 |    server never writes to it and never logs any token or key.
153 | 
154 | 4. **Using a different provider:** the code accepts any provider id and model id that the
155 |    CLI has credentials for — it passes `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID` and `HINTLAB_MODEL_ID` straight
156 |    to the SDK. Point HintLab at the provider you authenticated above with the matching
157 |    values, then confirm a real model call works:
158 | 
159 |    ```sh
160 |    HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=anthropic HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=claude-sonnet-4-5 npm start
161 |    # …then, in another shell, with the server running:
162 |    npm run check:agent     # makes a real model call on the chosen provider/model
163 |    ```
164 | 
165 |    (For the OpenRouter example, use `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=openrouter
166 |    HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=openrouter/auto`.)
167 | 
168 |    There is **no** `API_KEY` environment variable and no `config.apiKey`: the only
169 |    credential source is `~/.cline` (the providers file written by `cline auth`). The SDK
170 |    also honours the `CLINE_DIR` / `CLINE_DATA_DIR` environment variables to relocate its
171 |    config/data directory (HintLab uses them in `check:auth` to force an unauthenticated
172 |    provider without touching `~/.cline`).
173 | 
174 | ## 3. Environment variables
175 | 
176 | There is **no `.env` file and no dotenv loading** — `src/config.ts` reads `process.env`
177 | directly. Set them inline (`VAR=value npm start`) or export them. Every variable has a
178 | safe default.
179 | 
180 | | Variable | Default | Meaning |
181 | |----------|---------|---------|
182 | | `PORT` | `3000` | HTTP port the server listens on |
183 | | `RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `5000` | Per-test run timeout (ms) |
184 | | `BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS` | `15000` | Build (`gcc`) timeout (ms) |
185 | | `MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` | `1048576` (1 MiB) | Max captured stdout/stderr bytes per process |
186 | | `HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID` | `cline-pass` | Provider id passed to `ClineCore` |
187 | | `HINTLAB_MODEL_ID` | `cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro` | Model id passed to `ClineCore` |
188 | | `AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000` (5 min) | Max time an agent turn (`start`/`send`) may run |
189 | | `SESSION_TTL_MS` | `1800000` (30 min) | Idle session lifetime before cleanup |
190 | | `SESSION_CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS` | `60000` (1 min) | How often the cleanup loop runs |
191 | | `HEARTBEAT_MS` | `15000` | SSE keep-alive heartbeat interval |
192 | | `CLINE_DIR` | (SDK: `$HOME/.cline`) | Relocates the Cline CLI config dir (used by `check:auth` to force an empty one) |
193 | | `CLINE_DATA_DIR` | (SDK: `$CLINE_DIR/data`) | Relocates the Cline CLI data dir (providers.json lives under it) |
194 | 
195 | (Internally the runner also reads `process.env.PATH` to build the minimal environment it
196 | hands to student code — that's the OS `PATH`, not an app setting. `CLINE_DIR` /
197 | `CLINE_DATA_DIR` are honoured by the Cline SDK itself, not by HintLab code.)

199 | ## 4. Install and run
200 | 
201 | ```sh
202 | git clone <repo-url> hintlab && cd hintlab
203 | npm install
204 | 
205 | npm start        # run once (tsx src/server.ts)
206 | npm run dev      # watch mode (tsx watch src/server.ts)
207 | ```
208 | 
209 | Open **http://localhost:3000/** (override the port with `PORT=3300 npm start`). The web
210 | UI is static (plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS, no build step) and is served from `web/`.
211 | 
212 | > The check scripts (`check:agent`, `check:web`, `check:auth`) hard-code port **3200**, so
213 | > don't run the server on 3200 while running them.
214 | 
215 | ### Demo walkthrough (sum-of-list)
216 | 
217 | 1. Pick **`sum-of-list`** from the drop-down. The statement ("Read space-separated
218 |    integers on one line and print their sum.") appears and the buggy starter is preloaded
219 |    into the editor (it loops `for i in range(1, len(nums))`, skipping the first number).
220 | 2. Click **Run & get hint**. The server runs the code in a fresh temp dir and the
221 |    **Test results** table appears — all 4 tests **FAIL** (`basic` got `5`, `single` got
222 |    `0`, `negatives` got `9`, `first-only-big` got `1`).
223 | 3. The **Tutor activity** feed streams live as the agent reads the files (`read_files`)
224 |    and re-runs the tests (`run_tests`).
225 | 4. A **Level 1: nudge** hint card appears (the level-1 agent turn starts automatically).
226 | 5. Press **Next hint** → **Level 2: where to look**, then **Next hint** again →
227 |    **Level 3: the concept**. The button disables while the tutor is busy, and after
228 |    level 3 the status shows **All hints given**.
229 | 6. At no point does the tutor write or show corrected code — you only ever see prose hints.
230 | 
231 | ## 5. npm scripts and checks
232 | 
233 | | Script | Command | What it does |
234 | |--------|---------|--------------|
235 | | `npm start` | `tsx src/server.ts` | Run the server once |
236 | | `npm run dev` | `tsx watch src/server.ts` | Run in watch mode (restarts on change) |
237 | | `npm run build` | `tsc` | Type-check and emit JS to `dist/` (per `tsconfig.json`) |
238 | | `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` | Type-check only, no output |
239 | | `npm run test:runner` | `tsx scripts/check-runner.ts` | Sandboxed runner checks — **no model call** |
240 | | `npm run check:agent` | `tsx scripts/check-agent.ts` | Allow-list + hint-guard unit tests + a **real model** e2e on `sum-of-list` |
241 | | `npm run check:web` | `tsx scripts/check-web.ts` | Static UI + SSE contract + a **real model** session |
242 | | `npm run check:auth` | `tsx scripts/check-auth.ts` | Proves the unauthenticated-tutor error path (no model call, no `~/.cline`) |

244 | - **`npm run typecheck`** — `tsc --noEmit` across `src/` and `scripts/`. No network, no model.
245 |   Pass = exit 0 with no output. A few seconds.
246 | - **`npm run test:runner`** — runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starters and
247 |   asserts the exact pass/fail of every test (sum-of-list 0/4, is-palindrome 2/4,
248 |   average-marks 1/3), plus a correct solution for each assignment, an infinite-loop program

390 | - **One `ClineCore`**, created lazily in **local backend mode**
391 |   (`ClineCore.create({ clientName: "hintlab", backendMode: "local" })`) and subscribed once;
392 |   reused across sessions.
393 | - **Start + send:** the first turn is
394 |   `cline.start({ interactive: true, prompt, config: {...}, toolPolicies, capabilities })`;
395 |   follow-up hint levels use `cline.send({ sessionId, prompt })`.
396 | - **Tool policies** (`toolPolicies()` in `src/agent.ts`): `run_commands`, `editor`,
397 |   `apply_patch`, `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` are
398 |   `{ enabled: false }`; `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `give_hint`, `run_tests` are
399 |   auto-approved.
400 | - **Approval** (`capabilities().requestToolApproval`): returns `{ approved: false }` for
401 |   everything, so any command attempt is blocked and surfaced as an `approval` (denied)
402 |   event — defence-in-depth on top of the disabled `run_commands` policy.
403 | - **`run_commands` allow-list** (`src/allowlist.ts`): first rejects any command containing
404 |   `; && || ` $ | > & newline CR * ?`, then requires an exact match of the whitelist — only
405 |   `python3 main.py`, `python3 main.py < input-*.txt`, `gcc -Wall -O0 main.c -o main`,
406 |   `./main`, `./main < input-*.txt`, and `cat (main.py|main.c|tests.json|input-*.txt)`. Since
407 |   `run_commands` runs **on the host**, this allow-list (plus the disabled policy) is the only
408 |   protection between the model and an arbitrary shell.
409 | - **Custom tools:** `give_hint` and `run_tests` are built with `createTool(...)` + zod
410 |   schemas and passed through `config.extraTools`. `give_hint` is the only hint sink (the
411 |   server-side guard runs inside its `execute`); `run_tests` runs student code through the
412 |   hardened server runner instead of the host shell.
413 | - **Events:** `cline.subscribe(handleCoreEvent)` maps SDK `agent_event`s (tool starts/ends,
414 |   done, error) and `status`/`ended` to the SSE allow-list; model text/reasoning are dropped.

416 |   code beyond a short identifier, or any line that looks like source code (control flow,
417 |   function calls, assignments, casts, indexing/slicing, comparisons, trailing semicolons).
418 |   A rejected hint becomes a tool error so the model rephrases without code.
419 | - **Sandboxed runner** (`src/runner.ts`): a fresh temp dir per run, per-test/build timeouts,
420 |   `detached:true` + process-group `SIGKILL` to reap child processes, an output cap
421 |   (`MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`), and a minimal environment — only `PATH`, `HOME` (set to the run's
422 |   temp dir) and `LANG` are set, so the server's `process.env` is not inherited. **It is not
423 |   OS-sandboxed yet:** student code still runs as the host user and could read any file that
424 |   user can read (including `~/.cline`); the temp dir is not a security boundary. Signal
425 |   reporting (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGABRT`, …) and cleanup of the temp dir are included (except the
426 |   agent's workdir, which is removed later at TTL).

437 |    protection; that's why the agent's own test execution goes through the custom `run_tests`

474 |   Node 22+ (see §1).

492 |   hint and the guard made it rephrase; you'll see `hint_rejected` in the feed.
